title: Covid-19 Tracker: Smart Outbreak Analysis Dashboard
image1Description: Real-time Data Visualization system integrated with government APIs for pandemic reporting

section1.heading: Inspiration
section1.content: During the COVID-19 crisis, the overwhelming and scattered nature of information made it difficult to filter facts from noise. I believe that 'Data as a Source of Truth' is the best tool for building public confidence. This inspired me to develop a systematic dashboard for outbreak statistics, allowing citizens to track the latest situation and make informed decisions regarding their safety and daily planning with precision and timeliness.

section2.heading: Concept and Design
section2.content: I designed the web application as a Data Visualization tool focused on simplicity and accessibility. The system provides insights at both the national and provincial levels, focusing on four key metrics: New Cases, Accumulated Cases, Recoveries, and Deaths. It features an intelligent search system that allows users to drill down into specific areas to clearly assess local risk levels.

section3.heading: Challenges and Solutions
section3.content: The main challenge was ensuring data reliability and frequent updates. I integrated the system with the Ministry of Public Health's Open API to fetch data directly from government sources. To address API latency and the risk of source downtime, I structured a scalable data-fetching architecture. This ensures the system can process and display the latest information efficiently, even during high-traffic periods.

section4.heading: Opportunities for Further Development
section4.content: This project could evolve into a 'Public Health Surveillance Platform' by incorporating geospatial Heatmaps to visualize virus clusters more clearly. Future plans include transitioning from direct API calls to a Data Caching and local storage architecture. This will enhance system stability (High Availability) and support advanced Data Analytics for forecasting future outbreak trends.
